title: Berglund Center hosts Roanoke's second fall career expo - NewsBreak
text:
By Michael Doti ,
2 hours ago
ROANOKE, Va. ( WFXR )- The Greater Roanoke Workforce Development Board hosted its second fall career expo at the Berglund Center, providing an opportunity for people in the Roanoke area to learn about who’s hiring.
A wide variety of employers set up booths to discuss job opportunities.
“I’m just looking for something that I can maybe turn into a career at some point,” Roanoke resident Shane Peterson said. “Just something that can get me financially stable.”
Experts said there is value in this year’s expo, as people have struggled during the tightening of the job market in Star City.
“It’s really hard to get a job now, all of a sudden, and here lately it’s really been hard to get a job,” Roanoke resident Loraisia Hartley said. “I’m here because I got my CNA license, and so I’m just trying to get deeper into the caregiving field and stuff like that.”
Business and development manager for the Greater Roanoke Workforce Development Board, Toni McLawhorn, said the job market is more difficult this year than last year, likely due to increased prices and costs of operations.
She said that also could be why a lot of people are hanging onto the job they have instead of searching for a new one.
“They say it’s always easier to find a job when you have a job,” McLawhorn said. “I would encourage people to stay in their job and look and make sure that what they’re going to consider moving to is really what they want to do.”
Despite these claims, new job opportunities do exist, and for those struggling to find them, this was the perfect chance to come and discover something right.
“We’ve actually got a great job market here in Roanoke,” Amber Bridges, the talent acquisition specialist at Munters, said. “Munters is actually expanding because we have a new facility that will be opening in the spring of 2026, so we’re adding about 270 jobs.”
“There’s going to be a lot of opportunity for jobs and advancement within Munters,” Adriana Hernandez, the senior Human Resources journalist for Munters, added.”
Applicants also appreciated the value of face-to-face conversations with employers.
“People have just told me, ‘It’s online and go look for that there,’” Roanoke resident Gabriel Gomez said. “Now I can actually talk to someone, and someone can give me a little more details about the job, and it’s really great.”
Virginia Career Works was also on-site, helping people research the companies and improve their resumes.
